concepts.what: Whole flexible endoscope in side view: control body, insertion tube, umbilical connection and distal tip, with ports and valves visible.
concepts.teaches: What a flexible endoscope is made of and where its channels, ports, valves and removable parts sit, so each reprocessing step can be located on it.

concepts.what: Cross-section or cutaway of the insertion tube showing several narrow channels of different diameters running its length.
concepts.teaches: Why endoscopes have multiple narrow channels of different diameters, some hard to access and easy to forget, each needing its own brush and connector.

concepts.what: Longitudinal section of an endoscope channel with biofilm layer adhering to the channel wall, and a brush contacting the wall.
concepts.teaches: Why only mechanical brushing removes biofilm; chemical disinfection and flushing do not penetrate it.

concepts.what: Endoscope cleaning brush of the correct diameter and length passing through a channel, with the handle and bristle head shown.
concepts.teaches: Why brush diameter and length must match the channel, and the brush must emerge visibly clean.

concepts.what: Flexible endoscope connected to a leak tester and immersed in water, with air bubbles escaping from a breach in the outer sheath.
concepts.teaches: How a leak test shows a breach before immersion, since a breached scope admits fluid into an interior that cannot be cleaned.

concepts.what: Automated endoscope reprocessor with lid open, a scope coiled in the basin and tubing connectors attached to its channels.
concepts.teaches: How every channel must be attached to the correct model-specific connector, since an unconnected channel is not perfused or disinfected.

concepts.what: Distal tip of a duodenoscope close-up, side-viewing, showing the elevator mechanism and its narrow recess, ideally open and closed.
concepts.teaches: Why the elevator recess is a documented outbreak site: it directs accessories, is narrow and mechanically complex, and is extremely difficult to clean.

concepts.what: Controlled drying and storage cabinet with flexible endoscopes hanging vertically and uncoiled, valves removed.
concepts.teaches: Why scopes are stored hanging vertically and uncoiled with valves removed so channels drain and dry, unlike coiled storage that retains fluid.
